newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Presidential poll campaign opens in Madagascar.
newsitem.headline: Presidential poll campaign opens in Madagascar.

text.p: Campaigning for the November 3 presidential election in Madagascar -- with a record 15 candidates -- opened quietly on Sunday. Election rallies would get under way later this week, campaign officials said.

Ex-president Albert Zafy, whose impeachment for alleged violation of the constitution led to the election, begins his re-election campaign in the capital, Antananarivo, while his predecessor as president, Didier Ratsiraka, is starting in his home area, the east coast port of Toamasina.

Retired admiral Ratsiraka, "father of the socialist revolution", recently returned from 19 months of voluntary exile in France to compete for the office from which he was ousted in 1993 after an unprecedented wave of political protest.

Former prime minister and current acting president Norbert Ratsirahonana and National Assembly president Pastor Richard Andriamanjato are also standing, as are two other former prime ministers and four former ministers.

All the candidates have told their supporters to act with dignity and to avoid unnecessary provocation of their opponents. Campaign organisers say they will be using local musical groups to build up a festival atmosphere at their meetings.

One effect of the launching of the election campaign is that no four-wheel-drive vehicles are available for hire anywhere in the country -- they have all been booked to enable candidates and their supporters to cope with the country's rough roads.
